incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT ALERT: Hosted API p99 latency > 10s and request queue growth > 12k. Autoscaler reports multiple failed GPU node launches. Paging maya (oncall) and infra team.

maya (oncall): seeing huge backlog on /v1/generate, p95 ~ 4s, p99 ~ 18s. Errors starting to spike (502/504). What's the earliest root cause?

sanjay (infra): autoscaler logs show AWS capacity-constraints for p4d-family in us-west-2; several launch attempts hit InsufficientInstanceCapacity. Also one launch failed with AMI boot error: 'failed to attach ENI'.

gina (runtime): runtime queues report KV cache saturation per worker and many requests queued in front-end ingress. Batching pools are hitting max batch size then queuing. Token throughput per-GPU down ~20% due to degraded kernels.

kevin (prod-sre): any chance the recent kernel change pushed a perf regression? If per-GPU throughput is down, queue grows even if launches succeed.

gina (runtime): rolled back the kernel patch yesterday for a small subset; those hosts show stable throughput. The new failures are mostly in newly-provisioned nodes failing to join the serving mesh.

devon (support): customers are reporting timeouts; ticket volume rising. Which customers are impacted? Carmen, can you surface the top affected tenants?

carmen (customer-success): earliest call: 3 enterprise customers in us-west region seeing sustained 5–20s delays. We're preemptively flagging SLA risk for Premium tier.

sanjay (infra): mitigation plan: 1) stop autoscaler from launching p4d instances and fallback to p3dn for short term; 2) drain unhealthy AMI/boot path; 3) request spare capacity from partner pool. Initiating step 1 now.

maya (oncall): do it. Also enable rate-limiter on non-paid routes and reduce per-request max_tokens for hosted API default. We should remove optional heavy routes (reranking) to reduce load.

gina (runtime): applied rate-limits to public free-tier routes and lowered default max_tokens to 512. Also toggled model-fallback policy to route to a smaller quantized variant for non-Premium customers. Expect immediate drop in queue growth within 3–5m.

incident-bot: NOTE: automatic rollback suppression triggered for 1775549983 rollout. Confirmed suppressed.

kevin (prod-sre): I'm seeing backlog drop from 12k -> 6.5k after rate-limits and fallback. p95 trending down to 2.1s, p99 still at ~9s. Need to get more capacity to bring p99 < 2s.

sanjay (infra): p3dn launches in progress (slower GPUs but available). Bringing 40 nodes up. Also opening a cloud support ticket for p4d capacity and requesting spot burst from partner region.

devon (support): outbound comms: drafting status note to customers: brief impact summary, mitigation in progress, ETA for stabilization ~45–60m. Carmen, review?

carmen (customer-success): LGTM. Add note about temporary degraded quality for fallback model and invite customers to request priority routing if they have strict latency needs.

maya (oncall): quick check: any error spike due to timeouts at API gateway or internal LB?

gina (runtime): API gateway 502 rate rose, but majority are 504 from workers timing out waiting in queue. Also saw a small set of worker OOMs when they attempted quantized model with older runtime — we've isolated and restarted those processes.

kevin (prod-sre): Next actions: 1) continue p3dn ramp until p4d capacity confirmed; 2) push hotfix to autoscaler to fallback faster on InsufficientInstanceCapacity errors and avoid repeated launch storms; 3) post-incident: add quota pre-warming and region capacity fallback policy.

sanjay (infra): implementing autoscaler change now — adjusting backoff and adding immediate fallback path. Will push as config flip (no deploy).

incident-bot: ACTION CREATED: AUTOSCALE-FALLBACK-1775554321 assigned to sanjay, priority P0.

maya (oncall): handing off to kevin for next 30m while I join customer calls. kevin, please own mitigation and runbook items.

kevin (prod-sre): taking over. I've contacted cloud rep for p4d capacity and watching p3dn ramp. If queue stabilizes under 2k and p99 < 3s, we'll mark incident steady state.

devon (support): update to customers sent at 1775554980: "We're experiencing elevated latency due to a GPU capacity shortage in us-west-2. We've applied rate-limits and temporary model fallbacks. We're working on bringing additional capacity; estimated stabilization 45–60m."

carmen (customer-success): several customers replied asking for more detail. I've provided links to status page and offered 1:1 update.

kevin (prod-sre): current numbers (1775556600): queue 1.8k, p95 1.9s, p99 2.8s, error-rate down from 7.2% -> 1.3%. Still some 504s for longer requests.

gina (runtime): creating follow-up tasks: - add per-route graceful-degradation rules - add early-reject thresholds for huge token requests - improve KV cache eviction to avoid per-GPU saturation.

maya (oncall): thanks everyone. I'll do a post-call with execs. kevin, handoff notes?

kevin (prod-sre): Handoff summary: - Root cause: AWS p4d capacity shortage + autoscaler slow/failure path causing launch storms; compounding factor: some new host AMI/ENI boot failures and degraded kernel on a subset. - Mitigations applied: rate-limits, default max_tokens lowered, fallback to smaller quantized model, disabled p4d launches and ramped p3dn, autoscaler config flip to increase backoff and enable immediate fallback. - Customer impact: Premium/Enterprise tenants in us-west saw elevated p95/p99 and some timeouts; support notified; CS outbound done. - Next steps: autoscaler hotfix (PR + revert test), AMI boot error postmortem, region capacity pre-warming, improve monitoring for InsufficientInstanceCapacity signals, update runbooks and SLA communications.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATED: status -> mitigation, incident commander -> kevin (prod-sre).

kevin (prod-sre): marking thread as monitored. Will post postmortem draft in #postmortems in ~24h.

maya (oncall): thanks team. I'll rejoin at 1775557921 for final sync.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED (monitored): queue stabilized and p99 < 3s at 1775557921. Please follow up with postmortem and RCA."
